# Project Closure Report Definition
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

A Project Closure Report is a formal record created at the end of a project or phase to confirm completion, summarize results, record outstanding items and handoff, and capture lessons for future work.

It typically explains:

- what the project set out to achieve;
- what was delivered and its acceptance status;
- how actual results compare with scope, schedule, cost, and quality plans;
- what remains open and who owns the next action;
- how handoff or transition was completed;
- what lessons should inform future work;
- how administrative and contractual closure was handled; and
- which approvals or signatures are recorded.

The report is part of the official project record. Its repository location must come from project evidence and must not be guessed.
